h1: The 7 Best Printers for Chromebooks and School Laptops, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Printers for Chromebooks: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 printers that suit Chromebooks, scored on driverless wireless printing, running cost, scanning and troubleshooting ease.
summary: The Epson EcoTank ET-2800 is the printer to buy for a Chromebook household that prints often, with refillable ink that keeps running costs down. The Brother DCP-L2640DW is the pick for text-heavy homework, the Brother Work Smart 1360 has a screen that helps when the connection drops, and the Epson ET-4800 adds a wired fallback. The HP DeskJet 4355 is the cheap starter.
intro: A Chromebook cannot install the driver disc that comes with an old printer. There is no disc drive, no downloadable Windows installer and no space for manufacturer software, so a printer either speaks a standard network printing language that Chrome OS understands or it does not print at all. That is the one buying rule that matters more than speed, ink cost or color, and it is the reason people end up returning perfectly good printers.

So this ranking begins with how each printer connects, then moves to running cost and daily convenience. We reviewed seven models from their listings, comparing wireless protocol support, scanning, duplex, ink system and what happens when the connection drops. None of the listings states Chrome OS certification, so we rank on standard wireless support and use, and we flag where a claim is open to doubt.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2800 Wireless Color All-in-One
products.verdict: A refillable-ink printer with standard wireless support, for households where the Chromebook prints every week.
products.description:
Epson's ET-2800 swaps cartridges for a refillable ink tank, adds scan and copy, and lists standard wireless protocol support. It sits in the $100 to $200 range and fits a small desk.

It takes the top spot because Chromebook households tend to print school assignments, forms and the occasional photo, which adds up in cartridge costs. Refillable bottles cut the cost per page considerably, and the printer rarely stops mid-assignment because of an empty cartridge. Standard wireless support means the Chromebook can find it on the network without a driver. It sits above the cheaper HP and Canon models because the running cost is the difference between a printer you tolerate and one you like.

Choose it if more than a couple of people print. The caveat is a higher upfront price, and the lack of a document feeder means multi-page scans are slow.
cons: Higher upfront price than cartridge models
products.idealFor: Chromebook households that print every week.
products.skipIf: You print only a few pages a month.

products.name: Brother DCP-L2640DW Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser Printer
products.verdict: A mono laser with duplex and a 250-sheet tray, for text-heavy assignments printed in bulk.
products.description:
Brother's DCP-L2640DW uses a monochrome laser engine with duplex printing, a 250-sheet paper tray and Alexa support, plus standard wireless protocol listing. It costs $200 to $500.

It ranks second because text assignments are the main job for most Chromebook users. Laser toner does not dry out or clog if the printer sits idle over a holiday, which is a common failure for inkjets in households that print in bursts. Duplex printing halves the paper for long readings, and the large tray means fewer reloads. The cost is no color, so science posters and photos need another solution.

Buy it if the Chromebook is mainly for school or work documents. Skip it if you need color for projects.
products.idealFor: Families printing lots of text-based assignments.
products.skipIf: Color projects are common in your house.

products.name: Brother Work Smart MFC-J1360DW Wireless Color Inkjet All-in-One
products.verdict: A small color display and automatic duplex make connection problems easier to solve.
products.description:
The Brother Work Smart MFC-J1360DW carries a 1.8 inch color display, automatic duplex printing, standard wireless protocol support and LC501 series ink cartridges. It falls in the $100 to $200 range.

It ranks third because the screen matters more than it sounds. When a Chromebook cannot find a printer, the usual cause is a network change or a dropped connection, and an on-device display lets you see the network name and reconnect without a phone app or a PC. Duplex printing is a bonus for schoolwork. The limit is cartridge ink, which costs more per page than a tank model.

Pick it if you want an easy-to-recover printer for a family. Skip it if ink cost is your main worry.
cons: Cartridge ink costs more per page
products.idealFor: Families who want an easy way to reconnect the printer.
products.skipIf: You print enough that cartridge costs add up.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-4800 Wireless All-in-One
products.verdict: Ink tank economics plus Ethernet and a feeder, for a home office with a Chromebook.
products.description:
Epson's ET-4800 uses the same cartridge-free ink system as the ET-2800 and adds an automatic document feeder, Ethernet alongside wireless, and fax. It costs $100 to $200 and lists standard wireless protocol support.

It ranks fourth, below the ET-2800, only because most Chromebook homes do not need the extras. Where it earns its place is the wired option: if Wi-Fi misbehaves, a cable to the router keeps the printer on the network, which stops the common problem of a printer disappearing from the list. The feeder lets a student scan a multi-page worksheet in one go.

Choose it if the printer sits near the router or doubles as a home office scanner. Skip it if you want the cheapest ink-tank option.
pros: Full scan, copy and fax set
products.idealFor: Chromebook home offices near the router.
products.skipIf: You want the smallest, cheapest tank printer.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS5320 All-in-One Wireless Printer with AirPrint
products.verdict: The listing advertises AirPrint, the nearest thing here to a confirmed driverless protocol.
products.description:
Canon's PIXMA TS5320 is a wireless all-in-one with AirPrint advertised, Alexa support and a standard cartridge inkjet engine. It is in the $100 to $200 range.

It lands fifth because AirPrint is a point in its favor. It is Apple's network printing standard, and a printer that supports it usually also supports the open protocols Chrome OS uses to find printers without a driver. That is an inference and not a certification, so confirm it on the setup screen. The cartridge system is the weak point for a household that prints often.

Buy it if you share the printer with iPhones and iPads as well as a Chromebook. Skip it if you want the lowest ink cost, where an EcoTank wins.
pros: Good for mixed Apple and Chrome homes
cons: Chrome OS support is not certified
products.idealFor: Homes that mix Chromebooks with iPhones and iPads.
products.skipIf: Running cost matters more than protocol.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A budget wireless printer for Chromebook homes with light printing needs.
products.description:
The DeskJet 4355 from HP is a compact wireless all-in-one with scan and copy, standard wireless protocol support and a 3-month Instant Ink trial. It is in the $50 to $100 range.

It ranks sixth because the low price comes with cartridge ink and a lighter-duty build. For a household that prints a few pages a week, the savings on the printer outweigh the cost of ink. The Instant Ink trial can lower ink costs for a time, but it is a subscription you need to manage.

Buy it for a light-duty Chromebook starter printer. Skip it if homework printing happens daily.
products.idealFor: Light printing in a budget Chromebook household.

products.award: Best Feeder at a Low Price
products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: A cheap printer with an automatic document feeder for multi-page scanning.
products.description:
Canon's PIXMA TR4720 includes an auto document feeder, a built-in fax, mobile printing support and standard wireless protocol listing. It costs $50 to $100.

It ranks last because most Chromebook households will use scanning less than printing, and the cartridge system makes printing more expensive over time. The feeder is useful for scanning permission slips and forms, and mobile printing lets phones join in. The fax is a legacy feature that will go unused.

Choose it if your Chromebook household scans paper often on a tight budget. Skip it if your priority is cheap printing.
products.idealFor: Families scanning paperwork on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You print mostly and scan rarely.

whatMatters.detail: Chrome OS finds printers over the network using standard protocols and does not install maker drivers. A printer that lists standard wireless protocol support or AirPrint is most likely to work. Check the listing for those words, and confirm on the setup screen that the Chromebook sees the printer.

Tank printers refill from bottles at a low cost per page, cartridge inkjets cost less up front but more over time, and lasers use toner that does not dry out. Choose by volume: tanks for frequent mixed printing, lasers for text, cartridges for rare use.

Duplex printing handles both sides automatically, which halves paper use for long readings. A bigger tray means fewer reloads during a homework rush. Look for the words automatic duplex rather than manual duplex.

Network changes are the usual cause of a printer vanishing from the Chromebook list. An Ethernet port or a small display makes recovery quick. Look for them if the printer sits far from the router or if several people share it.

A Chromebook has no scanning software of its own, so you often scan with a printer app or the web. A document feeder handles multi-page forms in one pass. If you only scan a page or two, a flatbed is enough.

faq.q: Will my Chromebook print without installing a driver?
faq.a: Usually yes, if the printer supports standard network printing. Open Settings, choose Printers, and add the printer from the list. If it does not show up, check that both devices are on the same network.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake with Chromebook printers?
faq.a: Buying a printer that depends on a Windows or Mac installer. Chromebooks cannot run those, so you need a network-ready printer. Check for wireless protocol or AirPrint support in the listing.

faq.q: Is an EcoTank worth it over a cheaper printer?
faq.a: If you print weekly, yes. The refillable ink cuts running cost and prevents mid-assignment shortages. If you print rarely, a cheaper cartridge printer costs less overall.

faq.q: How do I add a printer to a Chromebook?
faq.a: Connect the printer to Wi-Fi, then open Settings on the Chromebook and select Printers. Choose to add a printer, pick yours from the list and save. A test page confirms the link.

faq.q: Why does my printer disappear from the list?
faq.a: Usually a network change, a router restart or the printer going to sleep. Reconnect the printer to the same Wi-Fi network as the Chromebook, or use an Ethernet cable if the model has a port.

faq.q: Can I scan from a Chromebook?
faq.a: Yes, through the printer maker's app or a web scan page. Check your printer's listing for scan support, and use a document feeder model if you scan multi-page forms.

finalTake: The Epson EcoTank ET-2800 is the best printer for most Chromebook households, thanks to its standard wireless support and low ink cost. The Brother DCP-L2640DW is the pick for text-heavy schoolwork, the Brother MFC-J1360DW has the easiest recovery, and the ET-4800 adds a wired option. Start with the connection, then choose by how much you print.
